steps.text: Radiation is heat that travels as rays — no material needed. That's how the Sun's heat reaches us across empty space. Let's test it.
Turn on a heat source, then choose a colour to absorb its rays — try “Black Shirt”.
Dark colours absorb radiation and heat up fast. Now try a light colour — it reflects the rays and stays cooler.
Radiation needs no medium (unlike conduction and convection). Dark absorbs, light reflects — that's why we wear light colours in summer.

coach.mission: See how radiation heats dark and light colours differently.
